transcript.text: We had a power cut last night and now our Candy washer dryer is completely dead - no lights, nothing. Everything else in the house came back on. The plug fuse is fine, I swapped it. Help!

A power cut can sometimes leave an individual socket dead even if the rest of the house is fine, or trip a specific RCD/fuse for that circuit. The next step is to confirm whether the socket itself has power. Please plug a lamp or phone charger into that same socket and see if it works. Let me know what happens.
Tried that already - a lamp works fine in the same socket, so the socket has power. The washer-dryer is still completely dead.

Since the socket has confirmed power but the washer-dryer is still completely dead, we need to look at what happens between the plug and the internal electronics. 1. The mains plug or lead has become loose or damaged (vibration can work plugs loose over time).
2. The internal mains interference filter (the first component that receives power) has failed, often due to the surge from the power cut.
3. 1. Pull the plug out of the wall socket.
2. Check the three pins on the plug for any blackening or damage.
3. Push it back in firmly until it is fully seated.
4. Try to switch the machine on. Let me know if that restores power, or if it remains completely dead.
Ok, I've unplugged it and the pins look fine, no blackening. Pushed it back in firmly and it's still completely dead.

The next most likely cause—especially after a power cut—is that the internal mains interference filter (the first component inside the machine) has failed. This is a standard safety part designed to take the hit from surges. 1. Ensure the machine is unplugged.
2. Look at the rear panel. Is there a removable cover (usually held by screws) that reveals the thick wires coming in from the plug?
3. If you can see them, please check if those wires are loose, disconnected, or burnt at their connection point to the filter board. If the wires look secure and clean inside, we will need an engineer to test the internal components safely.

I'm not comfortable taking the back panel off or poking about with the internal wiring, so I won't do that. The plug and cable look fine from the outside though. Is there anything else I can check, or do I need an engineer?

Since the socket has power and the plug/lead look fine from the outside, but the machine is still completely dead after a power cut, the most likely cause is that the internal mains interference filter (the component inside the machine that takes the surge hit) has failed. This is an internal part that requires opening the casing to inspect or replace. Because you are not comfortable removing the back panel, and this involves working on the internal mains wiring which carries a lethal shock risk if done incorrectly, you will need to call an engineer. They can safely open the machine, check the filter and incoming connections, and replace the faulty part. Please do not attempt any further internal checks yourself given your comfort level with the task.
